title: Drinks
grammar: Can I have…? / Would you like…?

scene.speaker: nico
scene.bubble: After football we are SO thirsty! Water for Tomás, lemonade for me… and a little water bowl for Pip.
scene.intro: After football Nico and Tomás are SO thirsty! Can I have some water, please? says Tomás, and he drinks a big glass in one second. Can I have a lemonade? says Nico. And then, in a small voice: can I have a hot chocolate too? Pip only wants the cup — to sit in it. What can YOU ask for when you are thirsty? Say it politely and try it with your friends!

activities.title: Grammar · Would you like…?
activities.instructions: Read the sentences. Then choose the right word.

data.title: Would you like a drink?
data.intro: You ask for something with Can I have…? You offer something with Would you like…? Both are polite, and the exam loves them.
data.can: I can offer a drink with Would you like…? and answer Yes, please or No, thank you.

examples.text: I would like some grapes. Would you like to colour that ball?
Would you like an apple? — Yes, please. Here you are.
Astrid: Would you like some milk? — Nico: No, thank you. I would like water.
Would you like to play with my ball? — Yes, please!

rules: Would you like + a thing: Would you like an apple?
Would you like + to + verb: Would you like to play?
Two answers, and both are polite: Yes, please. / No, thank you.

items.sentence: Would you like ___ play with my ball?
